sources.facts: Fadakari and Andaroodi, University of Tehran field and archival study. The four-porch layout centers on an enclosed courtyard, the main entrance is to the north, and the qibla iwan leads to the domed prayer hall behind it.

National Museum of Asian Art, Myron Bement Smith Collection FSA.A.04 ref9927. The central clock is flanked by the two minarets commissioned by Nasir al-Din Shah. The courtyard tilework bears artist inscriptions.

Abipour, Karimian Sardashti and Foroozesh report a tiled, segmented main dome topped by a smaller gold form, minarets at the north portico, a clock added between them in 1322–1323 AH, and a rectangular court pool. Text only.
